## Open

### F-655 — An integration run exits on CI, not on a timeout or a flag

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · open_

An integration run does not need a timeout and does not need an exit flag: the framework already
derives it, `integration.exit` is `isCI()` in blong-gogo/src/load.ts, so
`CI=1 blong ./index.ts integration` runs the groups and returns with a status. Three runs were
wasted waiting on `timeout 150` before that was read. The same runs then exposed a second lesson
worth keeping: a column that holds JSON comes back as the text that was written or already parsed,
depending on the driver, and `String(parsed)` is `[object Object]`, which fails as a JSON syntax
error two files away from the cause. The checkpoint transcript is now read through one helper that
accepts both shapes.

### F-656 — A fixture pool without a reset lets test order decide a claim

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · open_

Two things made the agent realm's first groups pass for the wrong reason before they passed for the
right one. A fixture pool that only hands tickets out makes every test depend on the order the
groups ran in, so a claim in one group decided what a claim in the next one got; the pool now
answers `task.pool.reset` and each group starts from its first ticket. And a session leaves behind
by a step that used another worker id is a session this host cannot suspend or answer, so a lookup
by session had to name the worker too — `agent.session.find` takes `workerId`, and the resume
precondition compares it with the host on purpose. Both were silent: the first surfaced as a missing
ticket, the second as `resumed: false` from a session that was never ours.

### F-658 — A question lost its channel at the tool boundary

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · open_

The seam test found a chain of three things, none of which any single-realm test could see. The
agent dropped the ticket's channel at the tool boundary — `agentToolRun` called `agent.question.ask`
without `platform`/`account`/`conversationId`, so the question parked under a fallback conversation
id (`ticketId`) that no answer would ever name. Chat minted its own prompt id, so the id this realm
had already checkpointed could not be the id the answer quoted; `chat.prompt.ask` now takes an
optional `promptId` from the caller. And the checkpoint is written before the ask, so a delivery
that arrives in the microseconds between the two finds nobody parked yet — the test retries the
delivery, which is what a platform does with a retry, and the parked promise stays the authority on
which one counted. The lesson is that a cross-realm seam fails on the ids and the addressing, not on
the logic: each side was correct alone.

### F-659 — One stale suspended session without a checkpoint failed a whole suite

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · open_

A tick that resumed every waiting answer threw agent.checkpointMissing for a row left behind by an
earlier notify run, and that single error failed the session group and every step after it, which
read as a regression from an unrelated change. A session that cannot be replayed must be skipped and
logged, and recovery purges it once it is stale, because one bad row is not a reason to stop the
loop. Clear the rows a test run leaves behind when the path under test is being changed.

### F-660 — A contributed port that the process Service already carries is a duplicate

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · open_

Contributing k8sPorts http 8080 to make the gateway reachable produced a Service with the port
twice, because the generator appends rpc and http for every deployment and then appends the
contributed ports beside them. The gateway was reachable all along; what was missing from the run
was the kustomize realm itself, which loads only when the entry package declares
@feasibleone/blong-kustomize as a dependency. The symptoms of both were the same empty tree, so
verify the object before adding a key that names it.

### F-670 — A chat deployment started the ticket worker

> _2026-11-01 · realm/blong-agent · open_

The `slack` intent ran the agent worker, whose fixture tickets name an engine account the deployment
does not have; the tick asked a question through chat with it, the ask threw `slack.accountMissing`,
and the process died. The same worker recovery-scanned sessions left by tests and asked in their
simulated channels, which is where the `the conversation is not one the app can see` errors came
from. A conversation deployment claims no tickets, so `workerStart` is false there.

### F-671 — A colon in a prompt id broke every control that carried it

> _2026-11-01 · realm/blong-agent · open_

A platform carries a question id inside an interactive element own id, and that id is split on
colons to be read back: `chatPromptSubmit:<promptId>`. A prompt id derived from the channel as
`pick:slack:blong-bot:C0CD...` therefore shifted every field after it, so a submit arrived with the
prompt id `pick`, matched nothing parked, and was forwarded as an answer nobody waited for. The
visible symptom is that clicking does nothing and the next typed message claims the pending question
instead. Keep a prompt id free of the separator.

### F-672 — An event payload was written wider than its column

> _2026-11-01 · realm/blong-agent · open_

`agent_event.payloadJSON` is 8000 characters, and only one caller remembered to truncate: a suspend
or resume wrote a whole question or answer and the insert failed with Data too long for column
payloadJSON, taking down the run that was recording it. A trace field has one writer boundary, so
the truncation belongs in `agentEventAdd` where no caller can forget it.

## Resolved

### F-651 — A base adapter that skips super.connect leaves start pending

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

A base adapter that never calls super.connect() leaves its port queue without a loop, and the
platform's start then waits for a promise that never settles: the log still shows adapter.start and
adapter.ready, the listeners come up, and a tap test expires at thirty seconds with two server
handles open. This is what the first version of adapter.agent did, and the fixture task adapter
looked like the culprit only because it was the other base-less file in the tree; extending
adapter.http fixed it by accident, since http calls super.connect(). The fix in
core/blong-gogo/src/adapter/server/agent.ts is a start() that calls super.connect() before
super.start().

adapter.agent now connects in start(); the realm boots with agent.task and agent.engine attached

### F-653 — An upgrade built a gateway, and the gateway dialled every model

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

A bare `blong ./index.ts upgrade` in the agent realm ended with RequestError getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN
rpc-core on http://rpc-core:8091/rpc/ports/core/request and left agent_answer uncreated. The schema
was never the problem: `core/blong-server/orchestrator/subject/validation.ts` builds the gateway
validations for every `public: true` model and reads each spec with `handler[handlerName]({}, {})`,
a call through the handler proxy that names another namespace (`core.label.model`,
`core.translation.model`, `access.access.model`). The upgrade intent in `blong-gogo/src/load.ts` was
`{exit: true}` alone, so a migration run still built a gateway, and the gateway is what asks for
those validations — with no server started there was nothing to answer the call and the host stayed
a bare `rpc-core`. The first fix, `remote.canSkipSocket` in the realm's own upgrade block, worked
but answered the wrong question: the realm was buying in-process dispatch to make a step run that an
upgrade has no business running. The block now turns the serving components off — gateway,
rpcServer, apiGateway, restFs, systemDebug, mcp — the same set `cli` and `k8s` turn off (`D-713`),
and the realm flag is gone. Verified with the flag removed: the upgrade exits 0, no request leaves
the process, and all four tables exist.

### F-654 — An orchestrator cannot inject its persistence handlers by name

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · resolved_

Group 6's first group, test.agent.session, is wired and runs against the integration intent, but
every step that reaches persistence fails with Handler 'agentAnswerFind' not found. The call is made
from an orchestrator handler through its injected handler proxy, and that proxy only knows the
caller's own folder (F-641); a probe step calling agentSessionFind from the test layer passes, so
the handlers are registered and the fault is the scope, not the registry. Adding `db` to the
orchestrator's imports made the names resolve and every call throw Database not available, because
the handlers then ran on the orchestrator's port and this.config.context.queryBuilder belongs to the
db adapter's instance; that is reverted. The fix is to call persistence through the port the handler
answers on, which the dispatch already routes to destination db: a small db(method, params, $meta)
helper over port.dispatch, and every injected persistence name replaced with its dotted wire name
(agent.session.get, agent.checkpoint.add, agent.answer.find, ...). Separately,
orchestrator/session/agentTools.ts is refused by the watcher as a generic source file in a handler
group folder; it needs to be a library() injected into agentToolRun.

Fixed with the documented shape: only the adapter whose namespace differs from the method needs the
prefix, so db/agentSessionAdd resolves while taskNextTask stays bare; two of the three test steps
now pass.
